answer: Agents in a decentralized economy resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a copper-weighted bond that is deposited at a virtual wharf before any activity is permitted. Detection of cloned behavior triggers automatic forfeiture of the bond. Because creating additional identities demands fresh collateral rather than free duplication, an attacker must continuously replenish the dune-like pile of locked funds, making large-scale sybil campaigns prohibitively expensive compared with honest participation.
